name: BulCommerce
author: GDimitrov

sections.description:
• Invoices, credit notes, proforma invoices, non-fiscal sales documents and order confirmations.
  • Gap-free sequential 10-digit numbering, safe under concurrent orders.
  • VAT breakdown by rate (20%, 9%, 0%), for both VAT-inclusive pricing and WooCommerce’s own tax engine. Document totals always equal what the customer was charged; if they cannot, the document is not issued and you are alerted.
  • Automatic credit notes for refunds and cancellations. When a refund cannot be attributed to a single VAT rate, no document is guessed: you get an alert and choose the rate yourself.
  • Company details at checkout (classic and block checkout): company name, EIK with check-digit validation, VAT number verified with EU VIES, MOL and registered address.
  • Couriers: Econt, Speedy, Pigeon Express and BOX NOW. Delivery to office, parcel locker or address on the classic and the block checkout: locality search, office list and map, address in parts with the courier’s streets, price table or the courier’s live price with automatic fallback (capped at a maximum the buyer pays, if you set one), cash on delivery, waybills (create, change, print, cancel), tracking and optional completion on delivery.
  • Checkout: compact layout without the address fields for a courier delivery, delivery options as cards, tiles or rows with courier logos (one row per courier with BulCommerce Pro), side cart, minimum order with a progress bar, cash on delivery hidden per courier, selling to other countries.
  • A checkout form of your own: reorder, rename, show or hide each field – for billing and for delivery – and choose which must be filled in, on the classic and the block checkout.
  • Pickup from your own shop, or deliver it yourself with no courier – one location free, several with BulCommerce Pro.
  • The expected delivery date, shown on the order-received page, in the account, in the order e-mails or on the admin order screen, per courier (where the courier’s own API gives one).
  • A shipment-tracking page and a right-of-withdrawal page of your own ([bulcommerce_tracking] and [bulcommerce_withdrawal]) – a buyer finds their order by its number and e-mail, no account needed, for either one.
  • An admin warning as your EU cross-border sales approach the €10,000 OSS VAT threshold; companies from other EU countries with a VAT number confirmed in VIES get services without Bulgarian VAT (reverse charge) or goods as an intra-Community supply at 0%, each with its own legal basis on the invoice.
  • Fiscal receipts on a fiscal device through ErpNet.FP, the NRA audit file (Ordinance N-18), Microinvest export, a document archive and the accountant’s monthly e-mail.
  • Cash on delivery: payout report, the month’s deliveries at the shop’s expense and an optional risk check (НепоСтоп) – or BulCommerce Guard (free, beta), which checks against a shared risk network instead of your own key.
  • A restorable settings backup, free on the BulCommerce network: the plugin settings, every courier’s credentials and options, and the delivery methods in your shipping zones.
  • Card payments through Stripe (optional): the Payment Element with cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and local methods, 3-D Secure, saved cards, refunds from the order screen and a signed webhook. Works on the classic and the block checkout.
  • FluentCart instead of WooCommerce, or beside it: the same couriers at its checkout with the live price and the buyer’s own office, the waybill and its label from the order, the order confirmation, the invoice and the credit note in the same numbering, the NRA audit file holding both shops, and the cash on delivery of its orders in the same payout report. The accounts and the settings are entered once, for both.

Fonts

PDF documents use the Inter typeface by The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter), licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. A Latin, Cyrillic and Greek subset is bundled in assets/fonts/ together with the licence (OFL.txt); tools/build-font.php rebuilds it.

External services

The plugin works without any external service until you switch one on. What follows is every service it can contact, what it sends and when.

Econt Express (courier)

Used when you enable Econt: to load its localities and offices, to ask for a delivery price at the checkout, to create, cancel and track a waybill and to download the label. Requests go to https://ee.econt.com/services (or https://demo.econt.com/ee/services with the demo account) with the credentials you enter.

Sent when you use those features: your sender details, the recipient’s name, phone and e-mail, the chosen office or address, the parcel’s weight, count and description, the cash-on-delivery amount and the order number. Nothing is sent for orders delivered by another method.

Service by “Econt Express” OOD: https://www.econt.com/ – terms: https://www.econt.com/za-nas/obshti-uslovia – privacy: https://www.econt.com/politika-za-poveritelnost

Speedy (courier)

Used when you enable Speedy, for the same purposes and with the same kind of data as above. Requests go to https://api.speedy.bg/v1 with the credentials you enter.

Service by “Speedy” AD: https://www.speedy.bg/ – terms: https://www.speedy.bg/bg/terms-and-conditions – privacy: https://www.speedy.bg/bg/gdpr

Pigeon Express (courier)

Used when you enable Pigeon Express, for the same purposes and with the same kind of data as above. Requests go to the API address of the account you enter (its sandbox or its production address).

Service by “Pigeon Express”: https://pigeonexpress.com/ – terms: https://pigeonexpress.com/terms – privacy: https://pigeonexpress.com/privacy

VIES (VAT number check, European Commission)

Used when a buyer asks for a company invoice and VAT checking is on (it can be switched off in the settings, and then only the format is checked). The VAT number and its country code are sent to https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/rest-api/check-vat-number, which answers whether the number is registered and, when the country publishes them, the company name and address.

Service by the European Commission: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/ – legal notice: https://ec.europa.eu/info/legal-notice_en – privacy: https://commission.europa.eu/privacy-policy-websites-managed-european-commission_en

European Central Bank (exchange rates)

Used when “Invoices for orders in another currency” is on: the euro reference rates are downloaded from https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist-90d.xml (and the full file when an older rate is needed) to convert an order into euro. No data about your shop, your orders or your buyers is sent.

Service by the European Central Bank: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html – disclaimer and copyright: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/disclaimer/html/index.en.html – data protection: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/data-protection/html/index.en.html

НепоСтоп (cash-on-delivery risk check, optional add-on)

Off by default. It works only after you switch the add-on on and enter your own API key. Before a cash-on-delivery order the buyer’s phone number is sent to https://nepostop.com/api/v1 to ask how many of that phone’s parcels were not collected. If you also switch on reporting, the phone number and the waybill number of your cash-on-delivery shipments are sent after they are created, so their outcome adds to the shared history. Tell your buyers about this check in your privacy policy.

Service by НепоСтоп: https://nepostop.com/ – terms: https://nepostop.com/terms – privacy: https://nepostop.com/gdpr

BulCommerce Guard (shared cash-on-delivery risk network, optional add-on, beta)

Off by default. It works only after you switch the “BulCommerce Guard” add-on on. Before a cash-on-delivery order the buyer’s phone number is sent to https://wpsupporting.com/api/wp to ask how many of that phone’s parcels were not collected; the phone is hashed on the server. If auto-reporting is on, the phone, the waybill number and the outcome (delivered / returned) of your cash-on-delivery shipments are sent after they are final, so the shared history stays useful, together with your licence key and your site’s domain to identify the shop. The order screen can also report a customer or erase them from the network on request. Tell your buyers about this check in your privacy policy.

Service by wpsupporting (the makers of BulCommerce): https://wpsupporting.com/

BOX NOW

One more courier, used in the same way and with the same kind of data as the couriers above, and only after you switch it on and enter your account: BOX NOW (https://boxnow.bg/ – the public locker list at https://locationapi-production.boxnow.bg (tests https://locationapi-stage.boxnow.bg) and the Partner API at https://api-production.boxnow.bg, tests https://api-stage.boxnow.bg).

This package contains no licence check and no update server of its own.

Stripe (card payments, optional)

Off by default. It works only after you enable the Stripe payment method and enter your own Stripe API keys. When a buyer pays by card, their browser loads Stripe.js from https://js.stripe.com and the payment is created and confirmed through https://api.stripe.com with your secret key. Sent to Stripe for a payment: the amount and currency, the order number and key, the buyer’s e-mail (for the receipt) and the card details the buyer enters (the card data goes from the browser straight to Stripe – it never reaches your site). Stripe notifies your site of the payment’s outcome through a signed webhook. Card and payment processing is subject to Stripe’s terms.

Service by Stripe: https://stripe.com/ – terms: https://stripe.com/legal – privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

OpenStreetMap (map tiles, optional)

Off by default. When you choose to show a courier’s offices on a map, the buyer’s browser loads the map images from https://tile.openstreetmap.org when the map is shown, which sends the buyer’s IP address and browser details to OpenStreetMap. Nothing about the order or the buyer is sent.

Service by the OpenStreetMap Foundation: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ – tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ – privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Fiscal printer through ErpNet.FP (optional, local)

Off by default. When it is on, the plugin talks to the ErpNet.FP service at the address you enter, which is normally a computer in your own shop (for example http://localhost:8001). The sale’s items, amounts and payment type are sent so the device can print the receipt. This is your own local network, not a service of ours. ErpNet.FP is free software: https://github.com/erpnet/ErpNet.FP

The plugin makes no other external requests, and it collects no telemetry and no usage data.
sections.faq:
Where do I get help?

BulCommerce is made by wpsupporting. Product page: https://wpsupporting.com/store/bulcommerce – support: https://wpsupporting.com/contact or info@wpsupporting.com (support policy: https://wpsupporting.com/support-policy). Attach the diagnostic report from BulCommerce → Help.

Is the “sales document” a fiscal receipt?

No. A fiscal receipt must come from a registered fiscal device. The sales document is informational.

What happens to documents when I uninstall?

Deleting the plugin keeps your setup by default (company details, courier credentials, add-on settings and the delivery methods with their prices), so an accidental delete costs you nothing; caches and scheduled jobs are cleared. Issued invoices, credit notes and their numbering always stay – they are accounting records you must keep. If you want a completely clean removal, switch on “Also delete all settings when the plugin is deleted” in Settings first.

My site is behind Cloudflare or another CDN and the plugin’s logos/styles are blocked as “mixed content”.

This happens when the CDN terminates HTTPS and WordPress does not detect it, so it builds asset URLs as http:// on an https:// site. The plugin’s own assets follow the site address you set in Settings → General, so they are served over https as soon as that address is https. For everything else on the site (uploaded images, other plugins), tell WordPress it is behind an https proxy by adding this near the top of wp-config.php:

if ( isset( $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] ) && 'https' === $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] ) { $_SERVER['HTTPS'] = 'on'; }
sections.changelog:
1.6.2

  • New: what the law asks of an online shop, on the Help screen. The twelve duties a Bulgarian shop is inspected against – seven from the Electronic Commerce Act, five from the Consumer Protection Act – each with its article, what it requires in plain words, what can be seen of it from your own install, and the sanction worded as the act words it, with a link to the text. What is seen to be missing is counted on the dashboard. It never says your shop is compliant: the three answers are “in place”, “missing” and “yours to confirm”, because most of these duties live in words on pages the plugin does not own.
  • New: the withdrawal page is now the withdrawal function of art. 52a, which an online shop has had to carry since 24 September 2026. A line in the footer of every page reading “Откажете се от договора тук”; a statement that takes the buyer’s name and the address the confirmation goes to, both offered already filled in; a button reading “Потвърждавам отказа” and nothing else; and a confirmation sent at once, repeating what was sent with the date and the hour – which is the hour the withdrawal counts as made. The footer link can be switched off by a shop whose own menu carries one.
  • New: how much is left to free delivery, in the side cart. A line and a bar above the total that fills as the buyer adds things and turns green when the threshold is reached, with your own wording if you want it. The amount comes from your own free-shipping method and counts the money that method counts, the coupon subtracted where it subtracts one, so the panel never promises what the checkout will not keep.
  • FluentCart: four add-ons that were WooCommerce’s alone now work there too – cash on delivery by courier (the per-courier rules, and the courier’s own answer about collecting cash at a parcel locker), the cash-on-delivery risk check, BulCommerce Guard, and the export of the orders of a period, which now carries both shops with a column naming which is which. A shop selling through both was setting these for one half of itself without being told.
  • Sameday is now part of BulCommerce Pro. It arrived free in 1.6.0 and said on its own screen that it would become part of Pro from the next version; this is that version. Econt, Speedy, BOX NOW and Pigeon Express stay free, with everything they do today. A shop that was delivering with Sameday keeps its orders, its waybills and its settings untouched: the courier itself is simply no longer offered at the checkout until the paid edition is installed, and the shipping methods it had in your zones stop being available.
  • Fix: the withdrawal settings screen, the Help diagnostics and the dashboard died on a shop without WooCommerce, which is a shop this plugin now supports. Each asked WooCommerce a question there was nobody to answer.
  • Fix: the side cart’s switches – open when a product is added, the floating cart button, the “View cart” button – read as off on a shop that had never opened their screen, although all three are declared on. Switching the side cart on from its card gave a panel that never opened by itself and had no button.
  • Fix: a mistyped e-mail address on the withdrawal page was accepted in silence and the confirmation went to the address on the order instead. It is the buyer’s proof of the day and hour they withdrew, so a mistake is now said out loud.
  • The side cart is called “Странична количка” everywhere. Three screens named it, in two different ways, neither of them the words a shop owner uses.

1.6.1

  • New: BulCommerce in FluentCart. A shop selling through FluentCart gets what a WooCommerce shop gets, out of the same accounts and settings entered once: your couriers at its checkout with the live price, delivery to an office, an address or a parcel locker with the buyer choosing the exact office; the waybill and its label from the order; the order confirmation, the invoice and the credit note, issued by themselves in the same numbering, a sale to a company in another EU member state included – with the reverse charge or the intra-Community supply named on the invoice, as on the WooCommerce side; the NRA audit file holding what both shops did in the month; the cash on delivery of its orders in the same payout report, settled the same way; the shipment tracking page and the right-of-withdrawal page, which find a FluentCart order by its number and the e-mail on it and are linked from the buyer’s own order page in FluentCart; and the fiscal receipt on a fiscal device through ErpNet.FP, printed by itself or from a fiscal screen of the plugin’s own, with its storno for a refund. An order paid through FluentCart’s own Stripe is invoiced with the Ordinance N-18 requisites and reported at the payment code you mapped.
  • New: BulCommerce no longer needs WooCommerce. A shop that sells only through FluentCart can run it: the couriers at its checkout, the waybills and labels, the documents and their PDFs, the NRA audit file and the cash-on-delivery report all work with FluentCart orders alone. What belongs to WooCommerce stays with it – its checkout settings, its order screens and the fiscal receipts – and the screens say so rather than showing you empty figures.
  • New (paid edition): waybills for FluentCart orders in a batch. Its order list takes no bulk action from a plugin, so this is a screen of its own: the orders still waiting to go out, what each one chose at the checkout, and one button that sends them all and collects the labels as one ZIP. Each order is dispatched through FluentCart itself, so the shipment, the tracking number and the e-mail to the customer are exactly what its own screen would have produced.
  • New (paid edition): card payments at a Bulgarian bank inside FluentCart – Borica, myPOS and DSK, on the same screens and with the same keys as the WooCommerce side.
  • New: a delivery with no price now says why, in the courier’s own words. A courier that will not price a parcel still leaves the delivery on offer, which was silent for the merchant: the last refusal of each method is now kept and shown on that courier’s screen, in Help and diagnostics and in the diagnostic report. A method that prices again drops off by itself.
  • New shops: every courier is asked for a real price as soon as the town is known, instead of showing your price table until the buyer picks an office. A shop already running keeps what it had, and your own choice outranks both.
  • Fix: paying by card on the compact checkout could end every order with “Invalid or missing payment details.” The checkout hides WooCommerce’s address fields and fills the address when the order is made, while a card gateway such as WooPayments reads those fields in the browser first. The address is now published with the order review and put into them.
  • Fix: above the order review, the number of items and the minimum-order bar were drawn once with the page, so a cart changed without a reload left them behind – a cart of 17.98 under “1 item” and “4.01 still to go”. They are refreshed with the order review now, the recommendation card with them.
  • Fix: a FluentCart shop with a euShipments method in a shipping zone met a fatal “Unknown courier” on its WooCommerce checkout.
  • Fix: a shop with thousands of orders or products could run out of memory exporting them – nearly ten thousand orders held 327 MB and now take 16 MB. An interrupted import carries on from where it stopped, and an import row naming one product by id and another by SKU no longer writes one product’s weight onto another.
  • Fix: the paid edition’s scheduled monthly file for your accountant could skip a month and never send it; a missed period now comes in the next file.
  • Fix: the export offered a period in UTC, so just after midnight on the first of the month it offered last month; a limit asked for is a total rather than a batch size; and a product left with duplicate meta rows by a bad import is counted once instead of doubling the list.
  • Fix: on the Add-ons screen a card could say it was switched on and be off again on reload, the three card-payment cards asked for settings that were already filled in, and a category chip counted cards that were filtered out.
  • New: Export and import. The product fields BulCommerce needs – weight, the three dimensions and the VAT rate on documents – go out as a CSV, are filled in a spreadsheet and come back. A shop with thousands of products is the one with the most weights missing, and it is the one that could not use a screen that edits fifty rows at a time. An import says what it would change before it changes anything: rows read, rows matched, products that would change, and the cells that are not numbers.
  • New: the orders of a period as a CSV, one row each, with the courier, the office or the address, the waybill, the cash on delivery, the payment method, the totals and the document number. For your accountant, and for checking a courier’s invoice against what was really collected.
  • New: BulCommerce in WordPress’s own toolbar, on the shop’s front as well as in the admin, so the settings for the checkout you are looking at are one click away.
  • The Add-ons screen is sorted into eight headings instead of five, none of them longer than five cards, and the headings are also a filter. Cards that said the same thing twice are merged: the accountant’s month is one card, how delivery looks at the checkout is one card, and a screen is one card whether or not the paid edition adds to it.
  • Fix: the NRA screen warned that your web address did not match the one filed with the NRA when it did – three of the seven ordinary ways of writing the same domain raised it. The two are compared as addresses now, not as text.
  • Fix: a finding raised once per order could fill the alert list and push the serious alerts out of it. Such findings are one alert that names the orders.
  • Fix (paid edition): four add-on cards still showed a padlock and a “See BulCommerce Pro” button to a shop that had bought it, and one of them linked to the shop.

1.6.0

  • New: Sameday, delivering to an address and to an easybox parcel locker, priced live at the checkout, with the waybill and its label made from the order. Sameday is free in this version and becomes part of BulCommerce Pro from the next one; the courier’s own screen says so.
  • New: a courier method added to a delivery zone starts accepting cash on delivery on its own, instead of quietly disappearing from the payment options. A method delivering to a parcel locker joins only where that courier really collects cash.
  • The setup wizard begins with your invoices. It asked for couriers, delivery, API access, payment and design, and never once for the company details that every invoice is printed with – although its own closing summary reported them. They are the first step now, and can be skipped.
  • Fix (Econt): the delivery price at the checkout after the courier’s daily cut-off, and all weekend. The price request alone did not retry with the next working day, so the checkout fell back to your own table while the waybill made afterwards got Econt’s real price: you were billed a price you had never quoted.
  • Fix (Microinvest export): a document exported as one line with the code of its main rate lost its VAT when that rate was 0%, and its taxable supply was reported as 0% – so the VAT ledger under-declared the VAT you charged.
  • Fix: annulling a document with “issue a new one” could leave both in force when the annulment protocol failed to be written, and the sale was then counted twice, in the month and in the NRA file. You are now told, with both numbers and the way out.
  • Fix: the checkout no longer reloads the delivery section while the buyer types the number, block, entrance or floor, which cut them off in the middle of a word.
  • Fix: a courier with no street list of its own shows a plain street field, instead of a search box whose suggestions never arrive.
  • Fix: with documents switched off, the checkout went on hiding WooCommerce’s own “Company name” field without putting ours in its place, so a company buyer had nowhere at all to write a company name.
  • Fix: the list of things needing your attention no longer repeats the same item every day. A condition that lasts keeps one place and says how long it has stood.
  • Fix (NRA): the export warns when the e-shop number is not in the form the NRA issues, and when the web address reported differs from the one your shop runs on – the two fields a file is refused for, which you learn only after the month has closed.
  • Fix: a credit note for a refund whose tax column was cleared no longer gives the money back with no VAT at all at a rate that charges it.
  • Fix: a fiscal receipt the device refused gives its sale number back, instead of leaving a gap in a series the ordinance wants unbroken.
  • Fix: the cash-on-delivery amount you type on a shipment is kept when the order had no preview to compare it with; the courier used to be sent to collect the whole order total instead.
  • Fix: a waybill records what the courier was actually told, so a delivery price folded into the cash on delivery is counted in the payout you expect and in the monthly courier costs.
  • Fix: cash-on-delivery risk checking matched a stored verdict on the masked phone number, which reads the same for different numbers.
  • Also: an impossible date is refused in the Microinvest period instead of exporting nothing without a word; unticking every document type in the accountant’s digest means every type, not none; the hourly courier-status job is no longer scheduled for a shop that only offers pickup from the shop; and uninstalling now deletes Sameday’s own settings too.

1.5.15

  • BulCommerce runs on PHP 8.0 again. Version 1.5.14 needed PHP 8.1, so shops on PHP 8.0 could not update to it and were left behind; the code no longer uses anything that needs 8.1, and the minimum is PHP 8.0. If your site is on an older PHP, your host can move it to 8.0 or newer for free.
  • Fix: the “Annul (Art. 116)” option on the order screen is shown openly instead of hidden behind a line that looked like plain text, with a word on what it does and when to leave the “issue a new document” tick off.
  • Fix: a fiscal receipt is no longer printed automatically for the full amount of an order that has a refund on it; the shop is told to issue it by hand for what was actually taken, so a partly refunded sale is not over-reported.
  • Fix: a cart taken over the free-shipping threshold by a downloadable or other virtual product now gets free delivery too, as WooCommerce’s own free shipping does.
  • Fix: the shipment-tracking page is kept out of shared caches, so a buyer’s name and address can never be served to another visitor behind a page cache.
  • Fix: the EU distance-sales total counts each order in the shop’s own calendar year, not in GMT, so sales near New Year fall in the right year.
  • Performance: the yearly distance-sales check and the “products with no weight” count no longer load the whole shop on an admin page; the hourly courier-status job runs only when a courier actually tracks statuses; and the first-version data migration no longer empties the whole object cache.
  • Fix: network-activating on a multisite now sets up every site, not only the main one.

1.5.14

  • Fix (Stripe): a double click on “Refund” could record two refunds in WooCommerce for one refund actually made. Both presses sent Stripe the same request, so the second was answered with the first one’s refund and taken for a second one; the doubled amount then went on into the credit note, the NRA audit file and the cash-on-delivery report. A retry of the same request is still never refunded twice.
  • Fix (Stripe): an order is marked paid only for its own amount and in its own currency, whichever route confirms it. A payment that was still settling, and one that collected more than the order total, used to complete the order in full with nothing but an alert; both are now held for you to check, as a payment that collected too little already was.
  • Fix (Stripe): a payment can no longer settle a second order. A shopper who placed two orders one after the other could, in a rare case, have the second marked paid on the first one’s card charge.
  • Fix (Stripe): a payment confirmation that arrives while the order is already being completed elsewhere is now asked for again instead of being dropped. It could leave the card charged and the order still waiting to be paid.
  • Fix: “Maximum the buyer pays” for the courier price applies only to the courier’s own live price, as it says it does. When the courier could not be reached and the price came from your own table instead, that table price was capped too and the shop quietly covered the difference.
  • Fix: clearing the delivery address at the checkout now clears it. A buyer who typed an address, thought better of it and emptied every field placed the order on the address they had just erased, and the waybill was printed for it.
  • New: when a courier cannot be reached to price the delivery, the order says so. The delivery is still offered at no charge, so that a courier briefly out of reach does not lose the order, and the courier bills the shop its own tariff on the waybill – but nothing on the order showed which orders those were, because a 0.00 courier fee looks the same as a free price from your table.
  • Fix: a site moved back to an older PHP now says what is wrong instead of showing a blank page. “Requires PHP” only stops an activation, so a site switched from PHP 8.1 to 8.0 with BulCommerce active lost the shop and wp-admin together, leaving no way in to switch the plugin off.
  • Fix: “Show the delivery in a pop-up” (Checkout design) is saved. The tick was discarded as it was being saved, so the pop-up never appeared however often it was switched on, and “Back to the default design” raised a PHP warning.
  • Fix: BulCommerce Guard’s daily reporting run is retired when Guard is switched off, instead of staying on the schedule for good with nothing to do.
  • Fix: deactivating or deleting the plugin also clears three scheduled jobs and two settings it used to leave behind.
  • New: the NRA audit file now warns when a sales document belongs to an order that is now a draft, the same as it already does for a cancelled order. An issued document is a sale, so it is still reported, but the shop is told – and shown what to do if the sale was not meant to stand (annul the document or issue a credit note), or if it was real (take the order out of draft).
  • The package no longer carries the development files (the dependency and static-analysis configuration), which were never read at run time.

1.5.13

  • Fix: the delivery options could collapse to zero width and spill across the order summary and the payment box on some custom checkouts (seen on the Rey theme), where the checkout column takes its width from its contents. The delivery block now always takes the full width of its column, so it can no longer overlap the rest of the page.
  • Fix: the once-a-day “products with no weight” notice no longer counts a variant that takes its weight from its parent product. A shop that sets the weight on the product and leaves the variants blank was told every day that its variants had none, though the courier was in fact pricing them by the real, inherited weight.
  • Fix: Speedy waybills no longer fail to generate when the delivery price is added to the cash on delivery. Speedy stopped allowing that option while the receiver is the courier-service payer; BulCommerce now sets the sender as the payer for it automatically (the standard “cash on delivery with the delivery added”), so the waybill goes through and the buyer still pays the delivery as part of the cash on delivery.
  • Fix: Apple Pay and Google Pay (Stripe wallets) now appear at the checkout, as their own express buttons above the card field, on both the classic and the block checkout. They are offered whenever “Wallets” is on in the Stripe settings and no longer only when Stripe Link is also on; a device without a usable wallet simply shows no button.
  • New: the Help page gathers more for a support request – the active theme, each courier’s key settings and when its local data was refreshed, the enabled payment methods, whether the site is served over HTTPS with OpenSSL, and the related active plugins – in a collapsible block with a one-click “Copy for support” button. It still carries no passwords or keys.
  • Fix (Pro): “Quick order” on a product with variants – whether the product is offered at all (its price and its category) is now judged on the product, not on the chosen variant. A variant carries neither the product’s categories nor a place in its price range, so a category limit used to hide nothing yet refuse every variant, and a price limit used to show the button yet refuse the dearer sizes, each only after the buyer had filled the form.
  • Fix (Pro): the [bulcommerce_quick_order] shortcode with a product id that names nothing (a deleted or mistyped one) now shows no button, instead of quietly standing the current page’s product in for the one asked for.
  • New (Pro): card payments through myPOS. The buyer chooses the card method and is taken to myPOS’s own secure page to pay, then returned to the shop – no card data ever passes through your site. The order is confirmed by a signed server-to-server notification, so a paid order is never lost if the buyer closes the tab. Works on the classic and the block checkout. Set it up with your myPOS store id, wallet, key index and key pair, with a separate sandbox store for testing.
  • New (Pro): card payments through Borica. Take cards on your bank’s virtual POS on Borica’s 3-D Secure gateway: the buyer pays on Borica’s own secure page and is returned to the shop, with the order confirmed by the signed response – no card data ever passes through your site. Works on the classic and the block checkout. Set it up with your terminal id, merchant id and key pair (a separate test terminal for the development gateway), and register the return address shown on its screen with your bank.

1.5.12

  • Fix: cash on delivery can be offered for an Econt or Pigeon parcel locker again. An Econtomat takes a card on its terminal, but the plugin had no switch for those two couriers, so cash on delivery disappeared at the checkout as soon as a locker was chosen and there was nothing anywhere to allow it. Each courier now has that switch in its settings, off until you turn it on.
  • Fix: BOX NOW’s “Allow cash on delivery to a parcel locker” showed as a text box asking you to type “no” or “yes”. It is a switch.
  • Fix: a cancellation that BOX NOW has taken but not yet carried out is no longer reported as one that may have failed. BOX NOW queues it and keeps showing the parcel as new until they process it; the waybill stays on the order until they confirm, and the status check records it then.
  • Fix: Econt now says on the settings screen, every time the setting is saved, when “How we pay the courier” needs a credit agreement your account does not have. Until now it said so only the first time that option was switched on, so an account that already had it found out from a refused waybill.
  • Fix: a courier delivery could vanish from the checkout the moment the buyer chose an office or locality. With the courier asked for its real price and no fallback price table, a courier that did not answer in time – a timeout, a credit-agreement gap, a brief outage – left the whole delivery section empty and “no delivery methods”, so the order could not be placed. The method now stays, priced when the courier can be reached or on the waybill.
  • New: with a courier asked for its real price, the shop is told once a day how many products carry no weight. A product without one is priced by the weight in the courier’s own settings, which is a guess: too low and the courier bills the difference on the waybill, too high and the delivery looks dearer than it is – and nothing said so, because a price did come back.
  • New (Pro): “Quick order” – a button beside “Add to cart” that takes a telephone and places the order there and then, with no cart, no checkout and no account. The shop calls back to settle the size, the delivery and the payment. Which fields it asks for, what they are called, where the button sits and which products it is offered on are all set on its own screen.
  • The “Checkout form” screen reads as one list again: the three marks are shown once with the icons themselves instead of being described in three paragraphs, every row is built the same way, and a field WooCommerce will not do without keeps both marks, shown on and locked, instead of a line of text squeezed into their place and wrapped onto two lines.
  • Fix: the checkout could refuse the order with “Please enter an address to continue.” and nothing on the page to put right, because the country field it asks for was not drawn at all. Once a courier with the locality picker or a pickup is chosen, the delivery is in Bulgaria, so the country is now answered at the moment the order is placed – whether this plugin’s compact checkout hid the field or the shop took WooCommerce’s address fields out with a checkout field editor. An empty country also left the order itself without one, so the invoice and the waybill had none either. Selling to other countries the buyer still chooses the country. The compact checkout also fills in an empty payer country even when the delivery country is already set.
  • Fix: a courier setting could be lost when several of them were saved at once, for example a map setting changed together with a logo.
  • Fix: with four kinds of delivery offered, the buttons lay out two by two on a phone instead of three on one line and the fourth alone on the next.
  • Fix: the delivery block in the “Standard” style follows the width it is given on a phone, as the other styles already did.
  • New: the document archive screen shows what the chosen period holds, and names the paid orders in it that have no document, with a link to each. Until now that was only worked out while the NRA audit file was being built, so a shop with that add-on off never learned.
  • The “Right of withdrawal” add-on is now called “Отказ от поръчка / продукт от поръчка”, which says what it does.

1.5.11

  • Fix: an Econt waybill to a company now carries the authorised person Econt requires for a legal entity, so the waybill is no longer refused. This completes the company-recipient change from 1.5.10.
  • Fix: the delivery options now lay themselves out by the width they are actually given, not by the width of the screen, so they fit the same way in any theme, in a narrow column, in the pop-up and in the admin preview. This ends a family of problems where on a phone the block was pushed off the right edge or the courier name was squeezed away on one theme but not another, and where a courier logo could overlap the price beside it.
  • Fix: delivery methods set up before October now lose the long dash in their name (“Econt – to office”). The name was saved in the shipping zone, so earlier updates could not reach it, and it is the name that appears on the order, in the e-mail and …

short_description: Bulgarian invoices, credit notes and company billing details for WooCommerce and FluentCart.
description:
• Invoices, credit notes, proforma invoices, non-fiscal sales documents and order confirmations.
  • Gap-free sequential 10-digit numbering, safe under concurrent orders.
  • VAT breakdown by rate (20%, 9%, 0%), for both VAT-inclusive pricing and WooCommerce’s own tax engine. Document totals always equal what the customer was charged; if they cannot, the document is not issued and you are alerted.
  • Automatic credit notes for refunds and cancellations. When a refund cannot be attributed to a single VAT rate, no document is guessed: you get an alert and choose the rate yourself.
  • Company details at checkout (classic and block checkout): company name, EIK with check-digit validation, VAT number verified with EU VIES, MOL and registered address.
  • Couriers: Econt, Speedy, Pigeon Express and BOX NOW. Delivery to office, parcel locker or address on the classic and the block checkout: locality search, office list and map, address in parts with the courier’s streets, price table or the courier’s live price with automatic fallback (capped at a maximum the buyer pays, if you set one), cash on delivery, waybills (create, change, print, cancel), tracking and optional completion on delivery.
  • Checkout: compact layout without the address fields for a courier delivery, delivery options as cards, tiles or rows with courier logos (one row per courier with BulCommerce Pro), side cart, minimum order with a progress bar, cash on delivery hidden per courier, selling to other countries.
  • A checkout form of your own: reorder, rename, show or hide each field – for billing and for delivery – and choose which must be filled in, on the classic and the block checkout.
  • Pickup from your own shop, or deliver it yourself with no courier – one location free, several with BulCommerce Pro.
  • The expected delivery date, shown on the order-received page, in the account, in the order e-mails or on the admin order screen, per courier (where the courier’s own API gives one).
  • A shipment-tracking page and a right-of-withdrawal page of your own ([bulcommerce_tracking] and [bulcommerce_withdrawal]) – a buyer finds their order by its number and e-mail, no account needed, for either one.
  • An admin warning as your EU cross-border sales approach the €10,000 OSS VAT threshold; companies from other EU countries with a VAT number confirmed in VIES get services without Bulgarian VAT (reverse charge) or goods as an intra-Community supply at 0%, each with its own legal basis on the invoice.
  • Fiscal receipts on a fiscal device through ErpNet.FP, the NRA audit file (Ordinance N-18), Microinvest export, a document archive and the accountant’s monthly e-mail.
  • Cash on delivery: payout report, the month’s deliveries at the shop’s expense and an optional risk check (НепоСтоп) – or BulCommerce Guard (free, beta), which checks against a shared risk network instead of your own key.
  • A restorable settings backup, free on the BulCommerce network: the plugin settings, every courier’s credentials and options, and the delivery methods in your shipping zones.
  • Card payments through Stripe (optional): the Payment Element with cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and local methods, 3-D Secure, saved cards, refunds from the order screen and a signed webhook. Works on the classic and the block checkout.
  • FluentCart instead of WooCommerce, or beside it: the same couriers at its checkout with the live price and the buyer’s own office, the waybill and its label from the order, the order confirmation, the invoice and the credit note in the same numbering, the NRA audit file holding both shops, and the cash on delivery of its orders in the same payout report. The accounts and the settings are entered once, for both.

Fonts

PDF documents use the Inter typeface by The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter), licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. A Latin, Cyrillic and Greek subset is bundled in assets/fonts/ together with the licence (OFL.txt); tools/build-font.php rebuilds it.

External services

The plugin works without any external service until you switch one on. What follows is every service it can contact, what it sends and when.

Econt Express (courier)

Used when you enable Econt: to load its localities and offices, to ask for a delivery price at the checkout, to create, cancel and track a waybill and to download the label. Requests go to https://ee.econt.com/services (or https://demo.econt.com/ee/services with the demo account) with the credentials you enter.

Sent when you use those features: your sender details, the recipient’s name, phone and e-mail, the chosen office or address, the parcel’s weight, count and description, the cash-on-delivery amount and the order number. Nothing is sent for orders delivered by another method.

Service by “Econt Express” OOD: https://www.econt.com/ – terms: https://www.econt.com/za-nas/obshti-uslovia – privacy: https://www.econt.com/politika-za-poveritelnost

Speedy (courier)

Used when you enable Speedy, for the same purposes and with the same kind of data as above. Requests go to https://api.speedy.bg/v1 with the credentials you enter.

Service by “Speedy” AD: https://www.speedy.bg/ – terms: https://www.speedy.bg/bg/terms-and-conditions – privacy: https://www.speedy.bg/bg/gdpr

Pigeon Express (courier)

Used when you enable Pigeon Express, for the same purposes and with the same kind of data as above. Requests go to the API address of the account you enter (its sandbox or its production address).

Service by “Pigeon Express”: https://pigeonexpress.com/ – terms: https://pigeonexpress.com/terms – privacy: https://pigeonexpress.com/privacy

VIES (VAT number check, European Commission)

Used when a buyer asks for a company invoice and VAT checking is on (it can be switched off in the settings, and then only the format is checked). The VAT number and its country code are sent to https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/rest-api/check-vat-number, which answers whether the number is registered and, when the country publishes them, the company name and address.

Service by the European Commission: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/ – legal notice: https://ec.europa.eu/info/legal-notice_en – privacy: https://commission.europa.eu/privacy-policy-websites-managed-european-commission_en

European Central Bank (exchange rates)

Used when “Invoices for orders in another currency” is on: the euro reference rates are downloaded from https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist-90d.xml (and the full file when an older rate is needed) to convert an order into euro. No data about your shop, your orders or your buyers is sent.

Service by the European Central Bank: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html – disclaimer and copyright: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/disclaimer/html/index.en.html – data protection: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/data-protection/html/index.en.html

НепоСтоп (cash-on-delivery risk check, optional add-on)

Off by default. It works only after you switch the add-on on and enter your own API key. Before a cash-on-delivery order the buyer’s phone number is sent to https://nepostop.com/api/v1 to ask how many of that phone’s parcels were not collected. If you also switch on reporting, the phone number and the waybill number of your cash-on-delivery shipments are sent after they are created, so their outcome adds to the shared history. Tell your buyers about this check in your privacy policy.

Service by НепоСтоп: https://nepostop.com/ – terms: https://nepostop.com/terms – privacy: https://nepostop.com/gdpr

BulCommerce Guard (shared cash-on-delivery risk network, optional add-on, beta)

Off by default. It works only after you switch the “BulCommerce Guard” add-on on. Before a cash-on-delivery order the buyer’s phone number is sent to https://wpsupporting.com/api/wp to ask how many of that phone’s parcels were not collected; the phone is hashed on the server. If auto-reporting is on, the phone, the waybill number and the outcome (delivered / returned) of your cash-on-delivery shipments are sent after they are final, so the shared history stays useful, together with your licence key and your site’s domain to identify the shop. The order screen can also report a customer or erase them from the network on request. Tell your buyers about this check in your privacy policy.

Service by wpsupporting (the makers of BulCommerce): https://wpsupporting.com/

BOX NOW

One more courier, used in the same way and with the same kind of data as the couriers above, and only after you switch it on and enter your account: BOX NOW (https://boxnow.bg/ – the public locker list at https://locationapi-production.boxnow.bg (tests https://locationapi-stage.boxnow.bg) and the Partner API at https://api-production.boxnow.bg, tests https://api-stage.boxnow.bg).

This package contains no licence check and no update server of its own.

Stripe (card payments, optional)

Off by default. It works only after you enable the Stripe payment method and enter your own Stripe API keys. When a buyer pays by card, their browser loads Stripe.js from https://js.stripe.com and the payment is created and confirmed through https://api.stripe.com with your secret key. Sent to Stripe for a payment: the amount and currency, the order number and key, the buyer’s e-mail (for the receipt) and the card details the buyer enters (the card data goes from the browser straight to Stripe – it never reaches your site). Stripe notifies your site of the payment’s outcome through a signed webhook. Card and payment processing is subject to Stripe’s terms.

Service by Stripe: https://stripe.com/ – terms: https://stripe.com/legal – privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

OpenStreetMap (map tiles, optional)

Off by default. When you choose to show a courier’s offices on a map, the buyer’s browser loads the map images from https://tile.openstreetmap.org when the map is shown, which sends the buyer’s IP address and browser details to OpenStreetMap. Nothing about the order or the buyer is sent.

Service by the OpenStreetMap Foundation: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ – tile usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ – privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Fiscal printer through ErpNet.FP (optional, local)

Off by default. When it is on, the plugin talks to the ErpNet.FP service at the address you enter, which is normally a computer in your own shop (for example http://localhost:8001). The sale’s items, amounts and payment type are sent so the device can print the receipt. This is your own local network, not a service of ours. ErpNet.FP is free software: https://github.com/erpnet/ErpNet.FP

The plugin makes no other external requests, and it collects no telemetry and no usage data.

upgrade_notice.1.6.2: Since 24 September 2026 an online shop must carry a withdrawal function on the site itself; the withdrawal page is now that function. A new Help screen lists what the Electronic Commerce Act and the Consumer Protection Act ask of a shop and what is missing from yours. Sameday moves to BulCommerce Pro, as its own screen said it would; Econt, Speedy, BOX NOW and Pigeon Express stay free.
upgrade_notice.1.6.1: BulCommerce now works in FluentCart too: couriers, waybills, documents, the NRA file and the payout report. On a WooCommerce shop: paying by card on the compact checkout could fail with "Invalid or missing payment details", a delivery with no price now says why, and the product weights and the orders of a period go out and come back as a spreadsheet.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: Sameday joins the couriers, free in this version. Worth having: Econt priced the delivery wrongly after its cut-off and all weekend, so you were billed a price you never quoted; the Microinvest export could lose a document's VAT; and the wizard now asks for your company details.
upgrade_notice.1.5.14: Card payment fixes worth having: a double click on "Refund" no longer records two refunds for one, and an order is marked paid only for its own amount and currency. Also: the courier price ceiling no longer caps your own table price, an emptied delivery address is no longer kept, and an older PHP says what is wrong instead of showing a blank page.
upgrade_notice.1.5.2: The compact checkout no longer flashes the address fields before hiding them.
upgrade_notice.1.5.1: The setup wizard opens on the first activation; Microinvest export and the NRA audit file are now on/off add-ons; a cleaner admin look and Bulgarian translation files for Loco.

screenshots.caption: The checkout: the couriers with a live price, delivery to an office, a parcel locker or an address, and the buyer picking the exact office. Classic and block checkout alike.
The checkout design screen: colours, shapes, logos and wording, with the real checkout beside it, updating as you change it.
Add-ons: every feature switched on or off with one click, each with its own settings.
The dashboard: revenue, cash on delivery owed and collected, waybills and labels, documents issued, orders by courier and by status.
Settings: company details for the documents, numbering, the couriers and their API access, and what happens to your data if the plugin is deleted.
Adding a courier: switch the integration on, enter its API access and add its methods to a shipping zone.
